title: Inkoxide document, version 1
description: A fully resolved, declarative document tree rendered to PDF by the Inkoxide engine. All lengths are PDF points (1/72 in); all colours are RGBA floats in [0, 1]. Unknown properties are errors.

fonts.description: Fonts the document references. Bytes are registered through the API (registerFont / options); this list lets validation fail early.

fallbackFonts.description: Font ids tried, in order, for characters missing from a run's font. Every id must be declared in `fonts`; an id listed again is skipped.

emojiImages.description: Emoji drawn as images: each key is one emoji sequence (`😀`, `👍🏽`, `🇫🇷`, `👩‍💻`; U+FE0F is ignored) of at most 64 bytes in UTF-8, each value the id of an image in the render option `images`. Where text has the sequence with emoji presentation, the image is drawn in its place, 1em high (the run's `size`), its bottom 0.1em below the baseline, and the sequence is its text for copying and search. A ZWJ sequence without an image tries its parts.

Link.description: Link target. `#id` jumps to the top of the first node with that `id` in the page body (the flow or an overlay): a node in a header or footer, or hidden by `display: none`, is not a destination (`UNKNOWN_ANCHOR` if there is none). Anything else must be an absolute URI with a scheme (`https:`, `mailto:`, …) and opens in the viewer. `javascript:` is rejected.

Bookmark.description: Document outline entry pointing at the top of its node. Entries appear in document order; an entry nests under the nearest earlier entry with a lower `level`. Flowing content only (not headers or footers).

Debug.description: A development aid: draws the element's boxes on top of the page, its margin (orange), border (yellow) and padding (green) as light fills and its content box as a blue outline, with its border-box size in points as a small label. On a text node it also outlines each line: its line box (dashed), its baseline, and the glyphs of each run on it, from the run font's ascender to its descender. The label is drawn with lines, so no text is added to the document. A box split across pages is drawn on each page it crosses. It changes the output: leave it off in production.

producer.description: The PDF producer, written to the PDF Info dictionary (and to the XMP metadata of PDF/A). Default `Inkoxide <version>`.

lang.description: BCP-47 language tag of the document, e.g. "en" or "en-GB".

creationDate.description: RFC 3339 timestamp written to the PDF Info dictionary. Overridden by the creationDate render option. When neither is set, no date is written (output stays deterministic).

pageMode.description: What the viewer shows when it opens the document: no panel (`useNone`), the bookmarks (`useOutlines`), page thumbnails (`useThumbs`) or the pages full screen (`fullScreen`). Default: `useOutlines` when the document has bookmarks, else `useNone`.

pageLayout.description: How the viewer lays out the pages: one at a time (`singlePage`), one scrolling column (`oneColumn`), two scrolling columns with odd pages on the left or right (`twoColumnLeft`, `twoColumnRight`), or two pages at a time with odd pages on the left or right (`twoPageLeft`, `twoPageRight`). Default: the viewer's own setting.

family.description: The family name. Text runs name fonts by `id`; text in SVG images is matched to the declared fonts by its `font-family` against this (ignoring ASCII case), then `weight` and `style`, as CSS matches fonts.

weight.description: The weight SVG text's `font-weight` is matched against.

style.description: The style SVG text's `font-style` is matched against.

NonNegative.description: A non-negative number of at most 1000000.

Fr.description: A flexible size, a share of the free space, of at most 1000000fr, like `"1fr"`.

Length.description: Points (within ±1000000), a percentage of the containing block (within ±10000%), or "auto". A percentage height needs a containing block with a definite height, as in CSS: a child of the page takes it of the page content height; in a header or footer, or in a box whose height is not set, it is `auto`.

LengthPercent.description: Points (within ±1000000) or a percentage of the containing block's width (within ±10000%). In `gap`, `rowGap` and `columnGap`, a percentage is of the box's own content box instead, as in CSS: a column gap of its width, a row gap of its height.

NonNegativeLength.description: A `Length` that is not negative: points (at most 1000000), a percentage of the containing block (at most 10000%), or "auto". A percentage height needs a containing block with a definite height, as for `Length`.

NonNegativeLengthPercent.description: A `LengthPercent` that is not negative: points (at most 1000000) or a percentage (at most 10000%), of what `LengthPercent` says.

Size.description: Page size in points. PDF/A, at any level, takes sides of 3 points or more: a render of a smaller page as PDF/A fails with `PDFA_CONFLICT` at the page's `size`.

PageSpec.description: A page template. Its content flows across as many physical pages as needed.

margin.description: `left + right` must be less than the page width and `top + bottom` less than its height; margins that leave no room for content are `OUT_OF_RANGE` at `margin`.

debug.description: Draws the boxes of the page (its margins and content area) and of every element on it, the header and footer included.

header.description: Laid out once at the full page width and painted at the top of every physical page (y = 0). Use padding to inset it. Size the top margin to leave room for it. `break` (other than its defaults) and `pageBreak` are not allowed in it, at any depth.

footer.description: Laid out once at the full page width and painted with its bottom edge on the bottom of every physical page. `break` (other than its defaults) and `pageBreak` are not allowed in it, at any depth.

Break.description: Pagination controls. They apply to flowing content only: on a header or footer, on a node in a table cell, or on any node inside these, a `break` with a value other than the defaults is `INVALID_VALUE`. For fixed overlays, see `fixed`. A box laid out as a row, a grid, wrapping or reversed moves to the next page whole when it fits on one; taller than a page, it splits between its rows (children whose extents overlap), each child continuing from the row's top. Content that cannot split (an image, a positioned, rotated, transformed or fixed node, table rows tied by a row span) is cut across pages when it is taller than a page.

before.description: `page` starts a new page before the node, unless it is at the top of one already. `INVALID_VALUE` inside a row, grid, wrapping or reversed box, or inside a positioned, rotated, transformed, floated or fixed node, or on an absolutely positioned or floated node: there it would do nothing.

after.description: `page` starts a new page after the node when in-flow content follows it: a break at the end of the flow adds no page. Allowed where `before` is.

inside.description: `avoid` keeps the node on one page: it moves to the next page whole when it does not fit. A node taller than a page splits anyway, and a forced page break inside it still starts a new page; the part before the break moves whole.

minPresenceAhead.description: Points of room the node needs from its top: when less is left on the page than this (or than its first unbreakable piece, when taller), the node moves to the next page. The node's own height counts, and nothing needs to follow it. On a box's first in-flow child it applies to the box too, so a box never leaves its top padding behind. `break.before: "page"` on a first child moves the box the same way.

fixed.description: Paint the node on every page of its flow. A child of the page with `position: "absolute"` is laid out on its own, against the page content box (`inset` and percentages are relative to one page's content box, inside the margins), takes no space and is painted over the flow, or under it when its `zIndex` is negative; no other pagination control applies to it or inside it, and it cannot hold a `pageBreak`. Any other fixed node is laid out in the flow, takes its space there once, and is painted at the same place on every page.

GridPlacement.description: 1-based CSS grid line placement. Negative lines count from the end; there is no line 0. Use `span` alone, with `start` or with `end`. With both `start` and `end`, `span` is ignored.

TrackSize.description: Grid track: a breadth, `{min, max}` (CSS `minmax()`; `min` cannot be fr) or `{fitContent}` (CSS `fit-content()`).

BorderRadius.description: One radius for every corner, or one per corner (a missing corner is square). Radii that would overlap are scaled down together, as in CSS.

BorderStyles.description: One style for every side, or one per side (an unset side is solid).

TransformOp.description: One transform function, as an object with exactly one key. Lengths are points or percentages of the node's own border box; angles are degrees, clockwise. Scale factors, `rotate` and matrix entries are within ±1000000; `skew` angles are within (−90, 90).

gap.description: Sets both rowGap and columnGap; either of those, when present, wins.

rowGap.description: A percentage is of the box's own content height, as in CSS. In a box whose height is not set, it is of the height of the content without the gaps, so it adds little: use points.

inset.description: top/right/bottom/left offsets for positioned boxes. A relative box (the default `position`) is moved by them before pagination, so pagination sees it where it is drawn: moved past the foot of a page, it moves to the next page or runs onto it.

gridTemplateAreas.description: Rows of whitespace-separated area names, as in CSS; a token of dots is an unnamed cell. Every row has the same number of cells and each area is a rectangle. At most 10000 cells (rows × columns; `OUT_OF_RANGE`).

gridArea.description: Name of an area in the parent's `gridTemplateAreas`; replaces `gridRow` and `gridColumn`, and cannot be combined with them (`INVALID_VALUE`).

justifyItems.description: Grid only: default inline-axis alignment of the items.

justifySelf.description: Grid only: inline-axis alignment of this item.

float.description: Children of a column box (not of a row, grid, wrapping or reversed box, and not a table cell itself) only; not with `position: absolute`. Floats the node to that side of its parent's content box, shrink-to-fit, at or below where it occurs, as CSS floats rectangles: lines of text after it wrap beside it, and boxes after it are narrowed to the room beside it, or move below it when their min-content width does not fit there. The parent's height includes its floats. Its children take no `flexGrow` or `flexBasis`, and it takes no `justifyContent` or `alignContent`. At most 1000 floated children per box. A float forces no page break: `break.before` or `break.after` `"page"` on it, or on a node inside it, and a `pageBreak` node inside it, are rejected. A float moves to the next page with the lines beside it, and is sliced when taller than a page.

clear.description: Puts the node's border box below the margin boxes of the earlier floats of its parent on these sides.

rotate.description: Degrees, clockwise, around the box centre.

transform.description: Transform functions, as in CSS: the list applies right to left, after `rotate`. Not on table cells. A transformed node moves to the next page as a whole.

transformOrigin.description: x and y of the origin of `rotate` and `transform` within the border box. Default `["50%", "50%"]`. Not on table cells.

zIndex.description: Paint order among siblings: higher paints later (above); equal values keep document order. Default 0. Not on table cells.

textAlign.description: text nodes only; `start`/`end` follow the paragraph direction. Default `start`.

lineHeight.description: text nodes only; multiplier of the largest run size on the line

lang.description: text nodes only; BCP-47, selects hyphenation patterns

whiteSpace.description: text nodes only. `normal` collapses spaces and keeps newlines as breaks (as `pre-line`); `pre-wrap` keeps spaces and tabs and wraps. As in CSS, only spaces, tabs and line breaks collapse: other space characters (thin, em, figure, no-break, …) keep their width, and only the breaking ones are break opportunities. `pre` and `pre-wrap` advance a tab to the next tab stop (CSS `tab-size: 8`): stops are 8 spaces of the tab's font apart, from the start of the line (a line `pre-wrap` wraps keeps the stops of the line it continues), and a tab narrower than half a `0` goes on to the next stop.

textWrap.description: text nodes only. How lines break: `wrap` fills each line in turn (first fit); `pretty` chooses the breaks over each stretch of the paragraph between forced breaks to make its lines even (Knuth and Plass's total fit, as TeX), with fewer hyphens, and lets the spaces of justified lines shrink by up to a third. A stretch with more than 20 000 break opportunities, or past 512 open breakpoints or 2 097 152 lines tried in the paragraph, falls back to `wrap`, as do `pre` and `nowrap` text, justified text without spaces, and a word wider than its line. `balance` is reserved.

textIndent.description: text nodes only; indent of the first line in points (negative: hanging indent)

direction.description: text nodes only; base direction of the paragraph (`auto`: from its first strong character). Right-to-left runs are reordered with the Unicode bidi algorithm in any direction.

orphans.description: text nodes only; minimum number of lines left at the bottom of a page when the paragraph breaks

widows.description: text nodes only; minimum number of lines carried to the top of the next page when the paragraph breaks

borderCollapse.description: Tables only. `collapse`: adjacent cell borders merge into one, drawn in the winner's style and colour: the wider wins, and at equal widths solid wins over dashed and dashed over dotted. `separate`: every cell draws its own borders, background and `borderRadius`, `borderSpacing` apart.

borderSpacing.description: Tables with `borderCollapse: separate` only: space between cells and around them, in points. Default 0.

text.description: Required unless `placeholder`, `image` or `note` is set; forbidden when one is.

link.description: Makes the run a link; the clickable area covers the run's glyphs on each line.

hyphenate.description: Overrides the text node's `hyphenate` for this run's words, in the node's language.

verticalAlign.description: Moves the run's baseline: `super` raises it and `sub` lowers it, by the offsets the font gives for superscripts and subscripts (OS/2), for text of the run's `size`. The size stays the run's own: give a superscript a smaller `size`. The line grows to fit the moved glyphs. An `image` run also takes `middle` (its middle at the baseline plus half the x-height of the run's font), `textTop` and `textBottom` (its top at the font's ascender, its bottom at its descender), `top` and `bottom` (its top or bottom at the line's), and a number: points its bottom sits above the baseline (negative: below).

fontFeatures.description: OpenType features by tag, as CSS `font-feature-settings`: 1 turns a feature on, 0 off, and a larger number picks an alternate (`{"tnum": 1, "liga": 0}`). Tags are four printable ASCII characters. A document may use at most 64 different sets of features.

note.description: A note in the line, in place of text: it takes no room, and its icon (20 pt square, the same at any zoom) hangs from the top of the line where the run is, on the page where the line starts. The run's `font` and `size` are the line's strut. Line breaking keeps it with the character before it, or after a space, the one after it.

InlineImage.description: An image in a line of text, as wide as `width` and as high as `height`, in points. With one of them, the other follows the image's aspect ratio; with neither, it is as high as the run's `size` (1em). The run's `font` and `size` still set the line's strut, and its `verticalAlign` places the image.

data.description: Inline image bytes (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP or SVG; the first frame of an animation), base64-encoded; a `data:<mime>;base64,` URL is also accepted.

objectPosition.description: Where the image sits in its box with `fit` `contain`, `cover` or `none` (CSS `object-position`); `fill` ignores it. Default centred.

alt.description: Alternative text: what copying, searching and screen readers get for the image.

style.description: The table places and sizes the cell: its columns set the width, and `height` and `minHeight` are minimums (the row grows to fit the content). The cell's own placement, size and effects are `STYLE_NOT_APPLICABLE`: `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `margin`, `position`, `inset`, `alignSelf`, `justifySelf`, `flexGrow`, `flexShrink`, `flexBasis`, `gridRow`, `gridColumn`, `gridArea`, `overflow`, `opacity`, `rotate`, `transform`, `transformOrigin`, `zIndex`, `float` and `clear`.

data.description: Inline image bytes (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP or SVG; the first frame of an animation), base64-encoded; a `data:<mime>;base64,` URL is also accepted.

objectPosition.description: Where the image sits in its box with `fit` `contain`, `cover` or `none` (CSS `object-position`); `fill` ignores it. Default centred.

ObjectPosition.description: Position of a fitted image in its box, per axis: a keyword, points from the left or top edge, or a percentage (that point of the image goes to that point of the box: `"0%"` is the start edge, `"100%"` the end edge). Points are within ±14400 and percentages within ±10000%. What falls outside the box is clipped.

BackgroundImage.description: An image painted behind the box's children and over its `backgroundColor`, under its borders. It fills the padding box (inside the borders), placed by `fit` and `objectPosition`, and is clipped to that box, rounded by `borderRadius`. A box split across pages is sliced, like its background colour.

data.description: Inline image bytes (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP or SVG; the first frame of an animation), base64-encoded; a `data:<mime>;base64,` URL is also accepted.

objectPosition.description: Where the image sits in the padding box with `fit` `contain`, `cover` or `none` (CSS `object-position`); `fill` ignores it. Default centred.

PageBreakNode.description: Starts a new page when in-flow content follows it: at the end of the flow it adds no page. Flowing content only: in a header, a footer, a table cell or a fixed overlay, and inside a row, grid, wrapping or reversed box, or inside a positioned, rotated, transformed, floated or fixed node, it is `INVALID_NODE`.

FieldNode.description: An interactive AcroForm field. `style` sizes and decorates its box (background, border, padding); the widget covers the content box. Without a width or height it takes an intrinsic size (text and select: 150 pt wide, one line, or three when multiline; list: 150 pt wide, one row per option up to four; checkbox and radio: `size` + 2 pt square).

Field.description: Fields with the same `name` are one field with several widgets (for example a field in a header, repeated on every page); only radio buttons may share a name with different values.

name.description: Field name; unique in the document except for the buttons of one radio group. Dots make groups: `address.street` is the field `street` in the group `address`, as in PDF's own field names. At most 32 parts of 1 to 128 characters, and 512 characters in all. A name used again, or used both for a field and for a group (`a` and `a.b`), is `DUPLICATE_ID`.

kind.description: `select` is a drop-down list, `list` a list box that shows several options at once

value.description: text: the initial text, at most `maxLength` characters (`OUT_OF_RANGE`); select and list: the selected option (one of `options`), or for a list with `multiSelect` an array of them, each at most once; radio: the value this button exports when selected, required and non-empty (`MISSING_FIELD`). A string is at most 8000 characters.

options.description: select and list only (required there): the choices, at most 1000 of at most 1000 characters each

multiSelect.description: list only: several options can be selected at once

password.description: text only; the value is neither shown nor stored

maxLength.description: text only; maximum number of characters

font.description: text, select and list (required there): a declared font for the value, with outlines (a font with colour bitmaps only is `INVALID_VALUE`). Its glyphs for the common Latin range are embedded so edits display.

size.description: font size; also the mark size of checkboxes and radio buttons

color.description: text and mark colour; default black

FieldFormat.description: Single-line, non-password text fields only: how the field shows and takes its value. The field shows `value` formatted; viewers format what the user types with the standard form scripts (`AFNumber_Format` and the like), which PDF/A leaves out (the formatted text and value stay). `value` must fit the format (`INVALID_VALUE`): a number or percent is `-?digits[.digits]` (at most 15 digits on each side; a percent is a fraction, `0.125` shows `12.50%`), a date `YYYY-MM-DD` with an optional `THH:MM[:SS]`, a time `HH:MM[:SS]` or a date with a time, `zip` 5 digits, `zipPlus4` 9, `phone` 10 and `ssn` 9. A key that does not apply to the `type` is `INVALID_VALUE`.

decimals.description: number and percent: digits after the decimal separator, rounded half away from zero; default 2

separators.description: number and percent: the thousands and decimal separators, by example; default `1,234.56`

negative.description: number: how a negative number shows: `-1.00`, `1.00` in red, `(1.00)` or `(1.00)` in red; default `minus`

currency.description: number: a currency symbol, shown as it is (add a space to separate it); no control characters, quotes or backslashes

currencyBefore.description: number: the currency goes before the number

pattern.description: date and time (required there): how the value shows, with `d`, `dd`, `ddd` (Mon), `dddd` (Monday), `m`, `mm`, `mmm` (Jan), `mmmm` (January), `yy`, `yyyy`, `H`, `HH` (0–23), `h`, `hh` (1–12), `M`, `MM` (minutes), `s`, `ss`, `t` (a/p), `tt` (am/pm) and the characters ` .,/:-`; a time shows only `H`, `h`, `M`, `s` and `t`. Names are English.

NoteNode.description: A text annotation: a sticky-note icon that opens its text in the viewer. It takes no space; its icon (20 pt square, the same at any zoom) sits at the top-left corner of its box, inside the page, on the page where the box starts. Under a transform, the icon stays upright and the same size: only its corner moves. In a header, a footer or a fixed element it is on every page.

author.description: Who wrote it; viewers show it as the note's title.

color.description: The icon's colour, also the colour viewers give the note (its alpha is not used); default yellow, [1, 0.82, 0.2, 1].

open.description: Whether viewers show the text when the document opens.

TrackBreadth.description: Grid track breadth: points, a percentage, "<n>fr", "auto", "min-content" or "max-content". Points and fr are at most 1000000.

TemplateTrack.description: Entry of a track template: a track, or CSS `repeat()` as `{repeat, tracks}`. `auto-fill`/`auto-fit` may appear once per list, and then every track in the list needs a fixed (points or percentage) minimum or maximum.

PageFilter.description: Pages that show the node, by physical page number (as the `pageNumber` placeholder). The node keeps its place in the layout on every page; it is only painted on the matching ones.

oneOf.description: 1-based page numbers; negative numbers count from the end (-1 is the last page)
